in subject and REFUSED WITH A MEASUREMENT rather than left open. The reading the handoff named as closest -- a verdict naming N members of a set where the record shows reads of fewer than N distinct members -- was built as a probe and run against a real Claude Code ledger, 29 turns carrying a claim. The counted-universal trigger matched 2 of them. One fires, and it is a false positive: `All 1086 ordered same-edge pairs refuted` was established by running tools/merge_pass.py, one command that checked all 1086, so the record holds 0 distinct file reads and no bulk result naming 1086 paths. That is the shape of the fault in the reading rather than a threshold to tune: in real work a claim over N items is discharged by a TOOL that examines the N items, so counting distinct reads against N is wrong by construction, and the bulk-read discharge the handoff asked for does not save it because merge_pass.py's output names no paths at all. The second match went silent only because the bulk heuristic happened to see 14 paths against N=7, a coin flip rather than a discriminant. Repairing it would mean judging whether a tool's output COVERS a prose-named set, which is the similarity judgement F12's row declines for this tree and the exact gate.unnamed_failure / gate.named_test overlap the handoff named as the risk. Prior art outside the tree agrees the fault is real and not visible in a trace: arXiv 2608.25869 measures anchoring in LLM judges through token log-probabilities, which a hook does not have, and published trace-audit tooling checks only that a claimed tool call happened, leaving quantified claims unaudited. Reopen this row if a corpus of real ledgers large enough to measure a rate becomes available; one session cannot produce one
